name: Sphinx rump passage and cavities
note: Mapped by the ARCE Sphinx Project; small, dead-end, documented.

name: Osiris Shaft
note: Three levels to about 30 m below the Khafre causeway, water at the bottom. Real, excavated, and the model's first genuinely subterranean structure.

name: Subterranean chamber of the Great Pyramid
ScanPyramids Big Void
note: Muon tomography, peer reviewed; position with error bars, inclination open.

name: ScanPyramids north-face corridor
note: Muon tomography confirmed by endoscope in 2023.

name: Cavity beneath the Sphinx's forepaws
note: Seismic refraction anomaly interpreted as a possible chamber about 5 m down; never excavated.

name: Khafre Project SAR shafts and complex
note: Eight vertical shafts to about 648 m with spiral structures and cubic chambers, and a complex to about 1.2 km, announced at a March 2025 press conference from SAR Doppler tomography. Not peer reviewed; radar specialists dispute that SAR can image hundreds of metres into limestone; the Egyptian antiquities authority rejected it. Modelled as a claim, rendered as such.

name: Hall of Records
note: Edgar Cayce's readings placed a chamber of Atlantean records under the Sphinx's paw. No physical evidence; registered so the viewer can show what the claim asserts.

name: Obelisk of Senusret I, Heliopolis
note: About 17 km north-east of Giza, in the same WGS84 datum and the Giza frame; the target of claim D1.

name: Sphinx Temple
note: The temple directly in front of the Sphinx's paws, surveyed by Nell and Ruggles in 2006; its measurement keys carry the prefix sphinx_temple, a key having no hyphens in it.

name: Valley temple of Khafre
note: The temple beside the Sphinx Temple, sharing the passage between the two; its measurement keys carry the prefix khafre_valley_temple.

name: Causeway of Khafre
note: The 495 m causeway running west-north-west from the valley temple up to Khafre's pyramid; its measurement keys carry the prefix khafre_causeway.

name: Head of the Delta, the barrage at El-Qanater el-Khayreya
note: A place rather than a monument: the point about 20 km north of Giza where the Nile divides, registered so claim D3 has something to take a bearing to.

name: Western corner of the Delta, Alexandria
note: A place rather than a monument, and a modern town standing for the Canopic mouth at the Delta's western limit.

name: Eastern corner of the Delta, Port Said
note: A place rather than a monument, and a modern town standing for the Pelusiac mouth at the Delta's eastern limit.
